area_m2.source: Elevator area 14.5 ft², both halves: Jane's All the World's Aircraft 1977-78, Cessna 172

chord_m.source: Chord aft of the hinge, 17 in, from the elevator's area and span

hinge_slope_per_rad.source: Hinge-moment slope read from NASA TN D-7149 Fig. 39a, a similar Cessna-type high-wing elevator; no 172 figure was found

up_deg.source: Cessna 172 elevator travel, 28° up; Cessna's maintenance figure as the elevator page took it, not yet checked against a copy

down_deg.source: Cessna 172 elevator travel, 23° down; Cessna's maintenance figure as the elevator page took it, not yet checked against a copy

gearing_rad_per_in.source: 7.8° of elevator per inch of yoke: the elevator's 51° of travel over a guessed 6.5 in of yoke travel

unbalance_inlb.source: Within Cessna's 0 to 43 in·lb trailing-edge-heavy allowance for both halves (Single Engine Structural Repair Manual 51-60-00, Table 1); no measured elevator was found

tab_ratio.source: How far the trim tab floats the elevator against it; the elevator page's estimate, no source recorded

tab_up_deg.source: Cessna 172 trim tab travel, 22° up; as the elevator page took it, no citation recorded, not yet checked against a copy

tab_down_deg.source: Cessna 172 trim tab travel, 19° down; as the elevator page took it, no citation recorded, not yet checked against a copy

alpha_slope_per_rad.source: Float slope Ch_alpha: no C172 figure found; a little under half of Ch_delta, the share plain flaps of this chord show in NACA TR 721 and Report 868 (not read from a copy). The 172's horn balances make it smaller, perhaps zero or negative

stall_factor.source: Share of the air's moments a stalled tail keeps: no published hinge moments past a tail's stall (the NACA data stop at it); the ailerons' figure, the owner's to tune

tau.source: The elevator's share of the tail section's angle: the flap-effectiveness chart (Raymer, Aircraft Design, from NACA plain-flap data) for an elevator about 40% of the tail's chord, that share guessed from the drawings

stall_deg.source: 0 turns the elevator's own stall off, leaving X-Plane's stalled share alone: the owner's call after the stall simulator (decision 17, 2026-11-09), which showed realistic stick speeds barely reach it and the drive's 18 lb limit hides it where they do. The code stays; 13 is the figure if it is tried again: a thin symmetric section stalls at about 12-14° (NACA 0009 and 0012, Abbott and von Doenhoff), erring early, since a deflected plain flap raises the section's most lift

stall_width_deg.source: The tail's stalled share grows from none to all over this many degrees past stall_deg; the elevator page's estimate

k_rev.source: With air from behind, the share of the deflection's hinge moment that turns over, so a free elevator runs to a stop (decision 17, 2026-11-09); no published figure

inertia_kgm2.source: Page only. Below a flat-plate estimate (Roskam; NASA CR)

wash_mps.source: Page only. Prop wash over the tail at full power parked, a rough slipstream estimate

damping_ratio.source: Page only. The free elevator's air damping, a rough estimate

area_m2.source: Aileron area 9.15 ft² each, from 18.30 ft² total: Jane's All the World's Aircraft 1977-78, Cessna 172, as the aileron page recalled it; not yet checked against a copy

chord_m.source: Chord aft of the hinge, 11 in, from a 64 in wing chord and a Frise hinge set back

hinge_slope_per_rad.source: Hinge-moment slope Ch_delta: a Frise aileron's range in NACA Report 868 and TR 721, not a 172's

alpha_slope_per_rad.source: Float slope Ch_alpha: a Frise aileron's range in NACA Report 868 and TR 721, not a 172's

up_deg.source: Cessna 172 aileron travel, 20° up; Service Manual figure as commonly quoted, not yet checked against a copy

down_deg.source: Cessna 172 aileron travel, 15° down; Service Manual figure as commonly quoted, not yet checked against a copy

wheel_deg.source: The Brunner's own wheel travel each way: its soft limits, 13000 counts, at CLS2Sim's 0.006646° per count

rim_m.source: Grip radius of the wheel, to be measured with a ruler

unbalance_inlb.source: The 172's ailerons carry balance weights (POH Section 7, as recalled); Cessna's balance limits are in SESRM 51-60-00 Table 1

stall_factor.source: Share of the hinge moment a stalled aileron keeps: no published post-stall hinge data; the owner's to tune

k_rev.source: With air from behind, the share of the deflection's hinge moment that turns over, so a free aileron runs to a stop (decision 17, 2026-11-09); no published figure

inertia_kgm2.source: Page only. Each aileron about its hinge, rough

wheel_inertia_kgm2.source: Page only. The wheel's own, rough

damping_ratio.source: Page only. The free ailerons' air damping, rough

wash_mps.source: Page only. Prop wash over the ailerons at full power parked: they sit outside most of the slipstream
